claims.text: At stage-1 cancellation lives in OrderServiceTests (new order, unknown id), OrderService.CancelOrderAsync (no status check; notifies), OrdersController.Cancel (calls it, returns a DTO) and FakeOrderRepository.Seed; all arrived in one commit.
review-comments-examples.md says its comments come from a PR adding cancellation; its first must-fix comment says a shipped order also gets moved to cancelled and ends with a question to the author.
The cancellation story in docs/team/story-example.md is about cancelling an unpaid order.
A diff tool usually shows files by path; reading tests first, then the layer closest to the behavior, then the rest, gives a reviewer the intended behavior before the code.
A 300-line PR approved in fifteen minutes with no comments more often means skimming than a perfect PR; the checklist turns a pass through the diff into a review.
OrderService.cs@stage-1 has a comment just above CancelOrderAsync (lines 25-28) describing the missing shipped check.
Sending all review comments together after finishing the PR is often easier for the author than comments arriving one at a time.
No test in DonHang.Tests@stage-1 calls OrdersController; Cancel's main work is the call to CancelOrderAsync; its [Authorize] and returned DTO have no test.
story-example.md acceptance criterion 3 lists paid, shipped and cancelled as statuses with no cancel button.
